To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we improve the ratio of SL problems with node costs and bonuses from $Ok \log k$ to \min p^ \log k, k \cdot O\log k$ and 2) we improve the best ratio known to $O\min ln n,ln^2 k$ for the Survivable Network problem when all edges form a star.

(i) the SL problem with unit costs and uniform demands can be approximated in polynomial time, while it remains \varOmega \ln n$ hard to do so for general demands, and (ii) the SN problem with star topologies admits a logarithmic ratio, improving over the ratio known for the more general case.

(1) the approximability status of SL is not fully resolved even for the most natural cases and (2) the approximable version of SL is a useful tool for solving the approximable variant of SN with stars.
